kurz: Why the sound structure of an ETF says nothing about its index rule, and what risks lie in thematic ETFs, leveraged and inverse products, ESG variants and backfilled index histories.

bloecke.md: On 8 September 2026, around 2,970 ETFs were listed on Deutsche Börse, plus 205 ETCs and 361 ETNs. A large part of this range came into being because the products could be sold. Solving an investment problem was not the reason for it. The label ETF describes a type of fund and is not a verdict on quality. An ETF reliably delivers the return of its index minus costs. Whether this index is sensibly constructed and how German tax law treats the product is a different question. The risks in this chapter all follow the same pattern. Segregated fund assets, tradability and transparency are in order; the problem lies in the content.

## Thematic ETFs

Instead of a whole market, a thematic fund tracks an investment theme such as hydrogen, cybersecurity, robotics, defence or semiconductors. Its index selects companies whose business model fits the keyword. The index itself therefore makes an active selection, which usually ends up with a few dozen stocks. In the third quarter of 2025, around $779 billion was invested in such funds worldwide, a three-year high.

Morningstar analysed the performance of these funds up to mid-2024. Around 94% survive the first year, three out of four survive ten years and only 45% survive fifteen years. More than half therefore disappear through closure or merger. In the three years to mid-2024, depending on the measure, only 9% to 25% of thematic funds beat a broad, low-cost global equity index. Taken together, over fifteen years around one tenth of the funds both survive and beat the market. With this hit rate, thematic funds are not suitable as the core of a portfolio.

## Launch date and price history

Providers launch whatever is selling at the moment, and by definition these are themes that have already performed well. At the end of February 2025, European defence ETFs managed around €3.7 billion. In 2026, the figure was around €17.5 billion, spread across 19 products, most of which were only launched in 2025. Since March 2025, net inflows into them have amounted to around €10.5 billion. In the second quarter of 2026, semiconductor ETFs took the top spot in thematic inflows with $3.19 billion.

These figures say nothing about whether defence or semiconductors are good investments. They show the sequence in which the price rises first, then the product is launched and after that the money flows in. Investors who can only buy a theme once there is an ETF for it are buying after the re-rating. A launch date one to two years after the price rise therefore says nothing about the quality of the product and is a reason to examine your own motivation.

Morningstar's *Mind the Gap* study compares fund returns with the money-weighted return of investors. In the decade to 31 December 2025, the funds achieved 9.9% a year and the average invested dollar 8.7%. The difference of 1.2 points arises solely from the timing and size of purchases and sales.

The gap widens with volatility. In the calmest fifth of funds it is 0.4 points, in the most volatile fifth 2.1 points. For broad US large-cap funds it is zero, for sector funds 1.2 points and for crypto ETFs in 2024 and 2025 around 14 points. For international equity ETFs it is 2.5 points, for conventional international equity funds 0.7 points. In almost all fund groups, ETFs show a larger gap than conventional funds. The magnitude is disputed. In the *Financial Analysts Journal* in 2026, Fulkerson, Jordan, Riley and Yan argue that poor timing costs less than claimed. What is undisputed is the direction of the relationship: the narrower and more volatile a product is, the more your own behaviour costs you.

## Leveraged ETFs

A 2x product promises twice the daily return, not twice the annual return. This difference is considerable. At the close of trading, the leveraged position is reset to the new fund assets. After a good day the fund buys more, after a bad day it sells. The product therefore necessarily trades procyclically, and this daily adjustment gives rise to path dependency.

bloecke.erklaerung: Because the previous day's value becomes the new base every day, the daily factors multiply. The leverage therefore acts on each daily movement and not on the overall change. Two price paths with the same starting point and end point thus lead to different results.

bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation, not market data. The index alternately rises by 10% and falls by 9.0909%, so that it is back at 100 after each pair. Both leverage directions lose value in the process.

bloecke.md:
After six steps, the index is back at exactly 100. The 2x product stands at 94.64, a loss of around 5.4%, and the inverse product likewise at 94.64. The same sequence with leverage of 3 ends at 84.51, which corresponds to a loss of around 15.5%.

The effect grows roughly with the square of the volatility. If the daily movement halves, around a quarter of the loss remains. Conversely, in a steadily rising market without setbacks, the same product delivers more than twice the index return over longer periods. An investor holding a leveraged product is therefore betting on two things at once: the right direction and low volatility.

## Inverse ETFs

An inverse ETF tracks the daily return with the opposite sign. It is therefore suitable for a bet over a few days, but not for hedging over months. In addition to path dependency, there is a second disadvantage. A permanent position against a market that rises in the long term also costs its expected return. This disadvantage grows with every day the position is held.

Two special features affect investors in Germany. The first concerns the legal form. Within the UCITS framework, leveraged equity ETFs in Europe are usually limited to a factor of 2. Anything advertised as 3x is usually an ETN or ETC, that is, a collateralised debt security with issuer risk and not segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen). The product type, recognisable from the three letters in the name, therefore determines what happens if the issuer becomes insolvent. The second special feature concerns tax. When the bank deducts tax, the 30% partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) under Section 20(1) InvStG (Investment Tax Act) is only granted if the investment conditions continuously commit to more than 50% equity participations (Section 2(6) InvStG). Some swap-based and special structures do not do this. The income is then fully taxable, even though the product is economically a bet on equities. Only if the investor proves that the fund exceeded the ratio throughout the calendar year can the partial exemption still be claimed in the tax return (Section 20(4) InvStG).

## Differences between ESG variants

Two products with the same three letters ESG in their name can differ greatly. A light filter only excludes what few investors want to hold anyway. A documented example from a broad world index excludes the 3% most CO2-intensive companies in each sector, as well as companies with severe ESG controversies or violations of the UN Global Compact principles, companies linked to controversial weapons and coal business models with a revenue share of 10% or more. Afterwards, the portfolio still contains a four-digit number of stocks. A best-in-class approach, by contrast, keeps only a small proportion of the companies in each sector. It produces a portfolio that differs markedly from the parent index, with deviations in both directions. These deviations stem from the concentration and have nothing to do with sustainability.

Regulation helps less with classification than is often assumed. Articles 8 and 9 of the SFDR (Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation) are transparency categories and not quality labels. Since September 2022, around 307 funds with around €175 billion have been downgraded from Article 9 to Article 8. In total, around 420 products changed their status, which corresponded to about 40% of the Article 9 category. The EU is working on a revision. The Commission proposal of 20 November 2025 provides for three voluntary categories (Sustainable, Transition, ESG Basics) with a minimum share of 70% of investments consistent with the strategy. The Council agreed on its negotiating mandate on 24 June 2026. The revision is not yet law.

The market for sustainable funds has also weakened. In 2025, net outflows from sustainable funds worldwide amounted to around $84 billion; in the first quarter of 2026, $3.5 billion flowed back in. In the same quarter there were only 17 new launches worldwide, a record low, and 50 closures. When buying, two questions should be kept separate. The first concerns the effect on your own portfolio, which can be measured (deviation from the parent index, concentration, costs, risk of closure). The second concerns the effect on the world, which, when units already in circulation are bought on the stock exchange, is at best indirect and empirically disputed.

bloecke.md:
## Dividend filters and niche indices

A dividend filter is a selection rule like any other. It sorts by the level of distributions or by distribution history and therefore inevitably leads to sector and country concentrations, mostly in financials, utilities and consumer staples, as well as to a value tilt. Whether this contains a premium is covered in the lessons on investment strategies. For the product itself, something else matters. Distributions are taxable in the year they are received, but in return they are deducted from the base return (Basisertrag) and so reduce the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale, Section 18(1) InvStG). In the accumulation phase, this means that tax deferral is lost; in the withdrawal phase, it can simplify liquidity planning.

For niche products, the main risk lies in small fund size. In the industry, an ETF with fund assets of around €100 million or more is considered cost-efficient and resistant to closure. Between €50 million and €100 million, operation becomes questionable, and below that it is rarely viable. In the US, around 230 funds were wound up in 2025, and the active ETFs that closed had existed for only around 1.75 years on average. In Europe, liquidations are much rarer, and reliable statistics are lacking. What makes a closure expensive is tax. The units are compulsorily sold at net asset value, and the gain is taxed under Section 19 InvStG, reduced by the advance lump sums recognised during the holding period. With the successor product, tax deferral starts again from zero. A merger into another fund, by contrast, usually continues without realisation. However, if the applicable partial exemption rate changes in the process, the units are deemed to have been sold and newly acquired under Section 22 InvStG.

## What backfilled histories can tell you

For almost every specialist index there is a chart that starts before the fund was launched, often even before the index itself was launched. Such a backfill is not a forgery. However, it is produced under a condition that is absent in live operation, because the rules were written when the data were already known. Indices whose backfill looked weak were never published. The charts in the brochures are therefore the best from an unknown number of attempts. The more degrees of freedom a rule has (thresholds, weight caps, rebalancing dates, sector filters), the more of them could be set to fit with hindsight.

This can be checked using two dates: since when the index has been calculated live and since when the fund has existed. The history before that is simulated; only the history after that is a real result. This result, too, needs time before it means anything. The ETF on the Solactive Gerd Kommer index, for example, has been on the market since June 2023 and had gained around 60% in value by the end of July 2026. This figure proves nothing either for or against the factor strategy behind it, because factor premiums can fail to materialise for ten years or longer.

- Find out since when the index has been calculated live and which part of the chart shown is backfilled.
- Look at the number of stocks in the index and the weight of the ten largest positions.
- Check how large the fund is and whether it is above or below the €100 million mark.
- Check whether the investment conditions continuously commit to more than 50% equity participations, so that the partial exemption applies.
- Work out what happens to the portfolio and how much tax is due if the product is liquidated in three years.

The fund structure says nothing about what an ETF contains. Segregated fund assets, exchange trading and daily transparency apply to a defence thematic fund just as much as to a world ETF. Diversification, costs, tax effects and prospects of success are determined solely by the index rule behind it. Every rule that is narrower than the market is an active decision, and there must be good reasons for it.

mitnehmen: An ETF is only the legal form of an investment; whether it is broadly diversified or resembles a single bet is decided by the selection rule of its index.
Thematic funds are usually only launched once a theme has already performed well; 55% disappeared within 15 years, and only around one tenth survived and beat the market.
Leveraged and inverse products deliver their leverage for only one day at a time and lose value in volatile sideways markets even when the index is unchanged.
Articles 8 and 9 are disclosure categories and not quality labels; around 307 funds have already been downgraded from 9 to 8.
In Germany, a liquidation has tax consequences, because it forces a sale at NAV, the gain is taxed under Section 19 InvStG and tax deferral ends.

begriffe.text: Property of daily reset leveraged and inverse products whose result depends on the path in between as well as on the starting and end level of the index. Fluctuations reduce the value, roughly in proportion to the square of the range of movement.

Adjustment of the leveraged position to the target leverage at the close of trading, based on the new fund assets. It forces purchases after price rises and sales after declines, and as a result the promised leverage applies for only one day.

ETF on an index that selects companies by a thematic keyword instead of by market coverage. It usually contains a few dozen stocks, is highly concentrated and is typically launched after a price rise.

Disclosure categories of the EU regulation on sustainability-related disclosures. Article 8 applies to products that promote environmental or social characteristics, Article 9 to those with a sustainable investment objective. The classification is not a quality label and can be changed at any time.

Price history of an index for periods before its live calculation, determined by applying today's rules to old data. Because the rules were drawn up with knowledge of these data, the backfill systematically overstates the prospects of success.
